keyVerseText: So the workmen wrought, and the work was perfected by them, and they set the house of God in his state, and strengthened it. the work: Heb. the healing went up upon the work
rootMeaning: The root of אֲרוּכָה (ʼărûwkâh) is אָרַךְ (ʼârak), which primarily means to lengthen, prolong, or make long. This root conveys the idea of extending or restoring something to its full and proper state. When applied as a feminine passive participle, it captures the sense of something being restored to soundness or health, emphasizing a process of healing and completion beyond mere physical lengthening.
usageInScripture: The word אֲרוּכָה appears six times in Scripture, consistently conveying the concept of healing, restoration, or being made whole. It is translated variously as 'perfected,' 'were made up,' and 'health,' reflecting both literal and figurative restoration. The usage includes physical healing, such as the healing of wounds, as well as broader restoration, including the repair of temple and city walls, illustrating its application to both personal and communal renewal.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲרוּכָה enriches our grasp of God's restorative work in Scripture. It highlights that divine healing is not merely the absence of disease or damage but a full restoration to wholeness and perfection. This aligns with the Christian hope of ultimate restoration in Christ, who heals and perfects both individuals and His people. The term's root meaning of lengthening and prolonging life also points to God's sustaining grace, which preserves and renews over time, assuring believers of ongoing spiritual health and restoration.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Chronicles 24:13, the phrase 'the work was perfected by them, and they set the house of God in his state, and strengthened it' uses אֲרוּכָה to describe the restoration process. The verse emphasizes that the workmen's efforts brought about a healing or completion of the temple, not just physical repair but a strengthening that restores God's house to its intended condition. This underscores the word's deep meaning of restoration as both healing and perfection, reflecting God's desire for His dwelling and people to be whole and sustained.
